correctness.rationale: The six disjoint support classes exhaust choices by whether each bipartition contains a selected original core. If both cores supported, all cores are observed. If only A is supported, all A pairs touched works; one untouched A pair can be forced only if a B pendant was selected; two untouched pairs stall. Symmetry supplies the B-only cases. If neither core is selected, selected leaves must leave at most one untouched pair per side to permit cross-forcing. Touched-pair choices contribute 2z+z², and subtracting the unique all-leaf choice produces A_n and B_n. These exhaustive mutually exclusive categories sum to the displayed polynomial. Direct independent power-domination propagation over every subset of five graph sizes confirmed all coefficients, including z² counts 22,15,19,9,12; formula and proof cover all p,q>=2, not the finite checks.
